newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia govt envisages 20 trln rbl tax from T-bills.
newsitem.headline: Russia govt envisages 20 trln rbl tax from T-bills.

text.p: The new draft of the 1997 budget submitted to the Duma last week, envisages raising 20 trillion roubles in taxes on Treasury bill operations, according to a copy of the draft obtained by Reuters on Monday.
Operations with government securities are currently not taxable, and earlier this month the State Duma lower house of parliament rejected a government proposal to impose a 15 percent tax on T-bills.
The document does not state the rate at which the newly proposed tax would be levied, but it was clear that it would be at the same rate as the original proposal.

The Duma rejected the original draft of the budget earlier this month, and asked the government to submit a new version, to be considered by a conciliation commission of representatives of the government and both houses of parliament.
The commission was due to start a preliminary examination of the revenue side of the budget later on Monday.
Other tax proposals include raising the income tax take on households to 7.54 trillion roubles in 1997 from a planned 5.88 trillion this year.
Proceeds from value-added tax are seen at 149.8 trillion roubles in 1997, up from a planned 113.3 trillion this year, although the government now expects only 79.7 trillion roubles in VAT this year.

Tax collection in general is running well below budgeted levels this year, prompting the International Monetary Fund this month to delay a decision on whether to pay out the latest tranche of Russia's $10 billion IMF loan.
The new draft did not change the proposed deficit, cutting both total revenue and and spending plans by 820 billion roubles.
